title: How later research cites work by smaller and larger teams
subtitle: A comparison of recent Columbia-linked research with Wu, Wang and Evans
open_reader_points: “For each author, we compared disruption ranks for their works on larger and smaller teams, adjusting for publication year and main OpenAlex topic without matching on either. Among 4,107 works, each doubling was associated with a rank 1.85 points lower, with a 95% interval of 0.27 to 3.43 points of decline. Without those adjustments on the same works, the decline was 1.73 points, with an interval of 0.46 to 3.01 points of decline.” It is unclear whether the second estimate still compares works by the same author. “Without matching on either” does not explain what the first estimate does.

“We ranked each score against other sampled works from the same year that qualified for the analysis. On the scale from 0 to 100, add the percentage with lower scores to half the percentage tied, using sampling weights for both. If weights total 100, with 40 below and 20 tied, the rank is 50.” The word “other” suggests leaving out the work being ranked. The example does not say whether that work is included in the tied weight.
